title: Need new terminology anchor for editable elements
body:
This is a follow up form a side discussion in #1873 :

I said: 

> Do we have a word for "elements that are normally writable/editable, but currently aren't because they're either in readonly or disabled state", or for "elements that are normally writable/editable, regardless of whether they currently aren't because of being either in readonly or disabled state"? If we don't, could we make something up? See w3c/csswg-drafts#285 for an instance of wanting this. (Also, let me know if I should raise that as a separate issue).

@domenic replied:

> > Do we have a word for "elements that are normally writable/editable, but currently aren't because they're either in readonly or disabled state"
> 
> I think "not mutable" might be what you're looking for?
> 
> >    "elements that are normally writable/editable, regardless of whether they currently aren't because of being either in readonly or disabled state"
> 
> "form controls"?

I followed up with:

> The terminology I'm considering establishing for the sake of CSS specs if I can't find anything better is this:
> 
> >    an editable element is either an editing host or a form control with normally mutable textual content such as textarea, even if this form control is in non mutable state.
> 
> It looks like it should work, but the phrasing doesn't look great to me, and I am kind of surprised there isn't already a word for this.

@domenic answered:

> Hmm I see. Yeah, I don't see any term for that. "Editable element" is probably not great since it collides with https://w3c.github.io/editing/execCommand.html#editable.
> 
> The closest I can find is "elements for which the [select()](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-textarea/input-select) method [applies](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-input-apply)." See the "applies" table to get an idea why.
